capture.final_message:
Use the finite-subset partial sums as the common representation.

First establish the key equivalence: an `NNReal` family `f` is summable exactly when the `ENNReal` supremum of its finite partial sums—namely `∑' b, ENNReal.ofNNReal (f b)`—is not `⊤`. The forward direction follows by coercing the finite `NNReal` sum; conversely, a finite ENNReal bound makes the increasing net of NNReal partial sums bounded and hence convergent.

Then derive the comparison statement from this equivalence. If `g b ≤ f b`, monotonicity of finite sums, and hence of `tsum` in `ENNReal`, gives
\[
\sum_b \operatorname{ofNNReal}(g_b)
\le
\sum_b \operatorname{ofNNReal}(f_b).
\]
Summability of `f` makes the right side non-top, so the left side is non-top; applying the key equivalence again yields summability of `g`.

Using finite-subset partial sums is important because `β` is arbitrary and need not come with an enumeration.
